unreg:coaching_and_governance_events.rederivation_notes: Own chain before reading the record: (a) a vacancy must exist or arise before Sep 1, 2027 (incumbent retirement/firing/departure hazard), otherwise every market settles No; (b) interim arrangement, and whether the interim coaches a full season and can audition for the job; (c) the AD/president run a search whose timing is set by the vacancy date and the season calendar; (d) candidate pool ranked on record, ties, cost (salary + buyout + roster/NIL budget), eligibility; (e) two-sided acceptance with competing vacancies; (f) leaks and announcement; (g) settlement: 'next permanent (non-interim)' coach 'selected before Sep 1, 2027', source not named, 'selected' undefined, coach-in-waiting not addressed. Required inputs: vacancy state, interim identity and the interim's in-season team performance, candidate record, ties, budget/buyouts, calendar, report ledger, unlisted/no-hire residual, rules text. One web check: Oregon's vacancy is real (Altman retired effective immediately on 2026-10-07; assistant Tony Stubblefield is interim for all of 2026-27; the national search starts after the season). Compared with the record: the record matches (b)-(g) in general, but its stages are written for a generic, fast in-season search. It treats interim-to-permanent only as an edge case and says that no game logic has any path to the outcome. That misses the main game-driven route for this vacancy: the interim's 2026-27 results. It also misses the roughly five-month deferred-search window and does not address the incumbent hazard for future speculative markets in this series.

findings.text: The record misses the interim-audition mechanism. The vacancy has an interim (Stubblefield) coaching the whole 2026-27 season before the search opens, and a strong interim season is a well-known route to the permanent job. The record lists 'Interim coach later made permanent' only under variants_and_edge_cases. It marks game_context_script NOT_APPLICABLE ('No game is played to settle the contract; game flow ... have no path to who is named head coach') and uses team ratings only to measure candidate track records (cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot KEEP_CONTEXT). The record needs an input for the interim's in-season performance against preseason expectation: fundamentals ratings, conference finish and NCAA bid/advancement through cbb.bracket_sim, plus interim-promotion base rates. That input should be secondary or primary for the interim's market.

The search-timing mechanism is generic and does not fit the sampled vacancy. In s1, 'most power-conference searches end within about two to four weeks of opening' and the coach_hire_field_residual decay 'in days since opening' both assume the search starts when the vacancy opens. For Oregon, the vacancy opened 2026-10-07 but the school said the search would begin after the season, so for about five months reports will be speculative and the unlisted-candidate mass will not decay. The record never states the actual vacancy facts (opening date, cause, interim name, announced search start). It needs a 'search start date versus vacancy date' field, and the conversion and residual curves need to be indexed to the search start, not the opening.

The no-hire mass is mis-specified for the series. cbb.coach_hire_field_residual measures no-hire mass as 'base rate of searches not concluding within the contract window (near 0 for long windows) plus probability the school names only an interim'. Nothing covers the case where no vacancy exists yet (a series template on a programme with a sitting coach) or where a coach-in-waiting is already named. An incumbent-departure hazard input (age, contract, performance, health, announced retirement) is needed for the archetype as labelled, which is 'coaching hires and programme governance decisions', not just this one vacancy.

The category mapping is strained and inconsistent. s3 lists 'opponent_matchup' in its categories, yet category_coverage marks opponent_matchup as GAP with no input. Show-cause orders are mapped to officiating_rules, and AD process is mapped to coaching_scheme. These mappings make coverage look fuller than it is.

The archetype label and blueprint do not fit. The label 'programme governance decisions' is broader than the only contract type, 'Next Coach'. catalog_entry.blueprint 'season_outcome' carries bracket and committee inputs that do not apply. A dedicated blueprint, or none, would be clearer.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: 'Stadium' is listed as an insider-reporting outlet, but Stadium's college basketball insider coverage has largely wound down, so this needs checking. The 'ESPN public JSON' source is described by its box-score note ('box scores, play-by-play and news') and is not shown to expose coaching-search reports with original timestamps. The report ledger will in practice depend on own_capture.

The rules quotes are verbatim and the settlement claims match the text: the permanent (non-interim) condition, the Sep 1, 2027 No-for-all clause, and no named source. The inference that a hire of an unlisted person settles every listed market No is correctly marked as an inference.

unreg:overtime_periods.rederivation_notes: Own chain before reading the record: rung N YES = tie at the end of regulation × (N−1) further ties after 5-minute OTs. P(regulation tie) is the integer pmf at 0 of the final margin. It depends on the expected margin (strength gap, home court, absences), the margin sd (possessions, three-point share), and end-game play: play for tie or win, foul when up 3, holding for the last shot, and late free-throw shooting by both teams. Repeat ties depend on OT possessions (about 1/8 of regulation), carried-over player and team fouls (bonus), fouled-out players and fatigue. Settlement: 'at least N overtime periods are played', 48-hour postponement rule, fair price on cancellation, no source named. These are game markets that trade during play, so the live score, clock and period state is the dominant input once a game is close late or in OT. Compared with the record: the stage structure matches. Differences: the record carries two primary inputs that compute the same thing; it has no in-play state; it drops team and lineup FT% as an input; and it misstates several magnitudes.

findings.text: There is a duplicate primary input. The catalog's existing cbb.ot_period_tie_chain measurement already defines 'P_tie_reg = integer pmf at margin 0 from the game's margin distribution ... with a discrete correction' as well as the repeat-tie chain. The new cbb.margin_integer_pmf_at_zero computes the same first-rung quantity, and both are labelled primary. Either mark the new input DUPLICATE_OF:cbb.ot_period_tie_chain or narrow the chain input to repeat ties only, so the same quantity is not counted twice.

In-game state is missing. The sampled market (status 'finalized') is a per-game ladder that presumably trades through the game. For the 2+ and 3+ rungs especially, the probability is essentially zero until a game is tied late or in OT, and is then driven by live score, clock, period, possession, fouls per player and bonus status. The record lists no live score/play-by-play feed with latency requirements and no in-play input; its required_data is entirely post-game or pregame. If SIFT prices these markets in play, this changes the required data. If it does not, the record should say so explicitly.

Free-throw shooting is missing as an input. Team and closing-lineup FT% decide whether intentional-foul sequences end level and drive scoring in bonus-heavy OT periods. The record itself says OT periods become 'more free-throw driven', and its interaction 5 relies on the 'leading team's best free-throw shooters'. Yet cbb.free_throw (in the blueprint) is not included or audited, and late_game_foul_script covers fouling policy, not the shooters' FT% distribution.

The magnitudes are inconsistent. The summary says each OT 'has about a fifth of regulation possessions', but 5/40 minutes is about one-eighth, and s4 itself says 'nine to ten possessions per team'. In s4, 'order 10 to 20 percent per period ... so 2+ and 3+ rungs are of order tenths and hundredths of a percent' is roughly 10× too small for 2+: with P(regulation tie) around 6% overall, 2+ is about 0.6–1.2% and 3+ about 0.06–0.25%. In s2, 'P(margin=0) is of order a few percent for evenly matched teams' understates it, since about 6% of all D1 games go to OT and even matchups must be above that average.

cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy is likely too weak to act as a coach-level secondary input. Situations with under 35 seconds left and trailing by 2 or 3 happen only a handful of times per coach-season, so shrinkage at n/(n+15) over 5 seasons will leave most coaches near the pooled rate. Treat it as context or tier-level unless a test shows otherwise.

Contract coverage is narrow. Only rung 3 (floor_strike 2.5) was sampled, so the existence and strike construction of the 1+ and 2+ rungs are inferred, not verified. The quotes are verbatim and the fair-price and 48-hour claims match the text.

Rule vintage (ot_u3) matters for the carryover input: team fouls carry into OT in the men's two-half format. This is correctly flagged, but the input's definition should state the rule version it assumes.

unreg:tournament_player_milestone.rederivation_notes: Own chain before reading the record: YES = union over all tournament player-games (First Four included) of {points ≥ 50} or {10+ in 3 of PTS/REB/AST/BLK/STL}. For each player-game: availability → minutes regime (close vs blowout, OT) → possessions (matchup tempo) → usage and FT trips → shooting heat (for 50) or a joint 5-stat draw (for triple-doubles) → scorer recording near 10. Exposure = bid × survival × availability, shared by teammates. Usage rises when a teammate is out. Field-level historical base rates matter: 50-point tournament games are extremely rare in the shot-clock/three-point era, and tournament triple-doubles are infrequent. Settlement: dates Mar 17 to Apr 6, 2026 'originally scheduled'; OT, source and corrections unstated. The market can also move within the tournament as the remaining bracket shrinks and once YES is hit. Compared with the record: the union, exposure and joint-stat structure match my chain. Missing: matchup tempo, teammate-absence usage shift, a historical field-level base rate as a calibration anchor, and in-tournament state. Two retained catalog inputs are market-derived.

findings.text: Pace is missing. The record covers pace_volume only with exposure and minutes, but possessions per game scale every count: a 50-point game or a 10-assist/10-rebound line is much more reachable against a fast opponent. cbb.tempo (in the blueprint) is not included, and the tail and triple-double measurements condition on minutes and usage but not on matchup possessions.

Market-derived values are smuggled in through retained catalog inputs. The catalog measurement for cbb.ot_model is 'Empirical OT frequency by closing spread and total bucket', and for cbb.blowout_garbage it is 'P(|margin| > 15/20/25) by spread'. Both are kept (KEEP_CONTEXT and KEEP_SECONDARY) without noting that they rely on market lines. They need to be redefined from fundamentals-only expected margin and possessions, for example via cbb.ratings_fundamentals or cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.

There is no field-level historical base rate input. The record defers calibration to per-player tails and lists the scarcity under mile_u4, but no input carries tournament-level frequencies: tournament triple-doubles per year, and 40+/45+/50+ tournament games by era with shot-clock and three-point adjustments. The tournament box-score dataset asks for only '15 tournaments', which almost certainly contains zero 50-point games and only a few triple-doubles. That anchor is needed to bound the union. The statement 'probability typically small (well under one half for 50+ points)' is too vague to sanity-check.

Teammate-absence redistribution is missing. A teammate's injury concentrates usage, rebounds and assists on the candidate, which raises tail probability. cbb.teammate_absence_shift (in the blueprint) is not included; star_injury_risk covers only the candidate's own absence.

In-tournament state is missing. Exposure measurement handles before and after Selection Sunday, but not the state during the tournament (remaining teams, games left, whether YES has already occurred). Since the market trades through the tournament window, that state should be part of the input set.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: 'Sports-Reference player game logs (triple-double finder)' needs checking, because the CBB player game/streak finder sits behind Stathead (paid) and CBB player game logs only start around 2010-11. The claim that a neutral-site scorekeeper 'removes the home inflation of assists and rebounds' is plausible but unmeasured; the record rightly lists environment as a GAP.

The rules quotes are verbatim, and the five-category / 3-of-5 / First Four claims match the text. The variant 'Games postponed outside the scheduled window ... are not covered' slightly overreads: the text says the tournament is 'originally scheduled' from those dates, which suggests postponed tournament games still count. It remains CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
